trigger: discovered while preparing Stage B of the 57-feature production; surfaced BEFORE spending the production effort

FINDING_1_MISSING_PERIODS.consequence: P/D cannot be built on the existing EMA surface. EMA34 and EMA89 must be produced first — they do not exist at any period on this surface.

FINDING_2_VALIDITY.holdout_consistent: HOLDOUT shows the same profile (EMA200 VALID 20.87%)

IMPLICATION.rule_in_force: the registration default is that AVAILABLE_INIT_SENSITIVE is NOT usable for claim evaluation
IMPLICATION.consequence: every EMA200-dependent feature has at most 20.81% valid support in DEV. For P/D that governs sig_p66/sig_d66 (cx200/dx200) and, through the ladder, the whole 12-column family.
IMPLICATION.compounding: this must further intersect with the opening-hour all-four requirement (53.72%) and with each feature own availability — the intersection was NOT computed here and will be lower still
IMPLICATION.not_a_defect: 47.93% INIT_SENSITIVE is not a bug. It is the honest consequence of resetting long-memory state at every UNOBSERVED_CONTAMINATED gap — exactly the discipline that prevents the legacy incremental-slice failure class.

WHAT_IS_UNAFFECTED: Stage A (Z x13, vol x3, suffix x4, body_wick, g* x4, tz_flip, vbo_up) needs no EMA200 and is not constrained by this finding
DECISION_SURFACED: whether to produce EMA34/EMA89 and the full P/D family given ~20.81% ceiling support, or to let the prespec consider a shallower-EMA grammar
not_done: no intersection of EMA validity with opening-hour support
